nodes.name: Arc-melting multiple precursor alloys
nodes.procedure: Alloy ingots of Fe₂₅₋ᵧ₋z Coᵧ Ce_z Al₇₅ (at%, where y, z = 0, 5 or 25) were firstly produced by arc-melting pure Fe (99.98%), Co (99.99%), Ce (99.5%) and Al (99.95%) metals with different atomic ratios in an Ar atmosphere. Specifically: (1) Fe₁₅Co₅Ce₅Al₇₅ by melting pure Fe, Co, Ce, and Al with atomic ratio 15:5:5:75; (2) Fe₂₀Co₅Al₇₅ (y=5, z=0); (3) Ce₂₅Al₇₅ (y=0, z=25).
nodes.source_text: Methods: Alloy ingots of Fe₂₅₋ᵧ₋z Coᵧ Ce_z Al₇₅ (at%, y, z = 0, 5 or 25) were firstly produced by arc-melting pure Fe (99.98%), Co (99.99%), Ce (99.5%) and Al (99.95%) metals...

nodes.name: Chemical dealloying
nodes.procedure: these eutectic Fe₁₅Co₅Ce₅Al₇₅ sheets are immersed in N₂-purged aqueous KOH solution to selectively etch less-noble Al component via a chemical dealloying process... chemically dealloyed to produce lamellar nanoporous FeCo/Ce-O composite precursor in N₂-purged 6 M KOH aqueous solution at 85°C until there do not observe any bubbles.
nodes.source_text: Methods: ...then chemically dealloyed to produce lamellar nanoporous FeCo/Ce-O composite precursor in N₂-purged 6 M KOH aqueous solution at 85°C until there do not observe any bubbles.

nodes.name: Thermal nitridation
nodes.procedure: the nanoporous FeCo/Ce-O sheets were further thermally treated in a mixed atmosphere of argon/ammonia (Ar/NH₃) with the molar ratio of 90: 10 at 600°C for 2 h to prepare self-supported lamellar and nanoporous FeCo/CeO₂₋ₓNₓ heterostructure electrode materials.

nodes.description: OER performance in O2-saturated 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To evaluate the electrocatalysis, all self-supported nanoporous electrode materials are directly used as working electrodes for electrochemical measurements, which are performed in O2-saturated 1 M KOH electrolyte in a classic three-electrode cell with a graphite counter electrode and an Ag/AgCl reference electrode... the nanoporous FeCo/CeO2−xNx has an ultralow onset overpotential of −186 mV... Tafel slope of 33 mV dec−1... at overpotential of 360 mV, the OER current density... dramatically increases to ·3940 mA cm−2

nodes.description: OER chronopotentiometry stability at 1.54 V vs RHE

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows bcc FeCo alloy with (110), (200), (211) planes at 44.6°, 64.7°, 82.4° and fcc CeO2−xNx with (111), (200), (220), (311) planes at 28.5°, 33.0°, 47.4°, 56.3°; FeCo peaks shift to higher angles and CeO2−xNx to lower angles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD characterization of nanoporous FeCo/CeO2−xNx verifies the composite structure with two sets of diffraction patterns at 2θ = 44.6°, 64.7°, 82.4° and 28.5°, 33.0°, 47.4°, 56.3°...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals periodically alternating nanoporous FeCo alloy/oxide and CeO2−xNx lamellas with interlamellar spacing of ~600 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b and Supplementary Figure 4 show representative scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of as-prepared nanoporous FeCo/CeO2−xNx composite electrode, displaying the unique architecture consisting of periodically alternating nanoporous FeCo alloy/oxide and CeO2−xNx lamellas with the interlamellar spacing of ~600 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows FeCo/CeO2−xNx interface with interplanar spacings of ~0.198 nm for Fe(110) and ~0.313 nm for CeO2(111); bcc Fe phase for FeCo and fcc CeO2 phase for CeO2−xNx confirmed by FFT and SAED.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d shows a typical high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image of FeCo/CeO2−xNx interface... interplanar spacings of ~0.198 nm and ~0.313 nm correspond to the lattice planes of Fe(110) and CeO2(111)...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows periodic distribution of Fe, Co in FeCo lamellas and Ce, O, N in CeO2−xNx lamellas with some Ce residue in FeCo regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The laminate composite structure of nanoporous FeCo/CeO2−xNx is also illustrated by its SEM energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings (Fig. 1g), where Fe, Co and Ce, O, N atoms periodically distribute...

properties.description: Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy maps for Fe, Co, O, N

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Co-Fe3O4 Eg at ~294 cm⁻¹, A1g at ~672 cm⁻¹; CeO2−xNx F2g at ~458 cm⁻¹ (redshift from 442 cm⁻¹ due to N-doping).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Owing to the transformation of Co·Fe2O3 into Co·Fe3O4, there appear two neoformative Raman bands... sharp peaks at ~294 and ~672 cm⁻¹ assigned to the Eg and A1g vibrational modes of Co-Fe3O4... Raman band at ~458 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the F2g vibrational mode of CeO2−xNx...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows surface Co and Fe mainly as Co³⁺, Co²⁺, Fe³⁺, Fe²⁺ due to Co·Fe3O4 layer; Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺ ratio 76/24; N 1s at 397.5 eV (Ce-N), 400.5 eV (adsorbed N), 403.6 eV (O-N); O 1s at 529.7 eV (O²⁻ in M-O) and 531.7 eV (oxygen defects Ov).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra show that the surface Co and Fe atoms of nanoporous FeCo/CeO2−xNx electrode are mainly in the oxidized states of Co³⁺, Co²⁺ and Fe³⁺, Fe²⁺ due to the presence of surface Co·Fe3O4 layer... The N 1s XPS spectrum with the M-N characteristic peak at 397.5 eV demonstrates the formation of Ce-N bonds... O 1s XPS spectrum... peaks at the binding energies of 529.7 and 531.7 eV.
